On 2026-10-03 Sat, the connected MicroFreak returned saved preset Microfreak/Preset/397 Imit, named Imit, category Keys, with populated sound data.

MIDI Control Center was open during both read-only transfers. Both completed, with matching headers and sound data and no detected protocol interference. This demonstrates coexistence for these downloads; simultaneous MCC transfers remain untested.
The patch was used in a recent GitP episode. The episode association is unspecified; the capture retains the existing name.
Captured patch files and reports are stored locally under assets/Microfreak-2026-10-03-slot-397-Imit/; the public repository contains the validation notes.
Original raw patch and capture manifest preserve the saved header and complete sound data.
Repeat-read manifest records a second device download whose complete raw content matched the original capture.

Imit preset export (.mfpz) was generated locally from the raw capture using Elektroid's serialized object format and a ZIP member named 0_preset. It was not downloaded through an installed Elektroid executable.

Validation report records the repeated-download comparison and the export's matching sound data. The existing garden parser reopened the export, recovered the name/category and parsed the parameter layout successfully.
Parameter inspection provides named raw parameter values. Display-scale conversions and sound interpretation are outside this validation.
The existing microfreak:download task can capture this populated saved slot directly over USB. It checks response sequence, operation and length for the header and every sound-data packet.
No preset write, rename, program change, restoration or memory-protection change was performed. The experiment read the saved preset rather than the current unsaved edit buffer.

The matching repeat read supports using the captured sound-data fingerprint to detect later changes before renaming. The manifests retain the complete fingerprints rather than relying on the slot name.
Parser round-trip validation establishes that the generated export preserves the captured sound data. Acceptance in MCC and successful device restoration are still untested.
Import the generated .mfpz into an MCC computer bank and verify its displayed metadata, without sending it to the device.
Choose a backed-up test slot for a restore test and compare the restored sound data with the original capture.
Build the reusable episode-capture mise task around the proven download path and validated export format.
Preview a convention-based rename when an episode date and patch order are available, then test the USB write on a backed-up slot.
Microfreak/CLI/Episode patch workflow tracks the broader implementation plan; Microfreak/CLI/Preset metadata over USB records protocol research.

Basic motivation: for GitP/A, ideally, I'd have the presets used in each episode delivered in Backblaze/B2 and a CDN and referenced from the podcast so people could download them. Indeed, you can see in some episodes, I already do this today. Towards this end, I'd like you to create a new Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth which would represent a single synth preset. The information inside of it should be similar to the kinds of things stored in the preset manager for microfreak as described in Microfreak/UG/04 Presets. Arturia does have their own piece of software for interacting with presets on the Microfreak, the Arturia MIDI Control Center, but it's a GUI application and as such it suck my life away like a vampire with all its clicking and dragging. I'd like to have a CLI/Tool application that I can reference in a new Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak which would describe how to use it to sync it. At first, I just want to model the preset information, but eventually, I want to also have the binary file stored in Backblaze/B2 as well and keep it relatively in sync with the knowledge garden. The goal is that each Music/Composition/Log entry should reference several presets, for example, Microfreak/Preset/397 Imit would have a description of what that preset is, whether it's custom or factory, and any details about it. Then I - or my agents - can use autocomplete to reference those in the garden logs that document my music improv sessions. The original idea here came from Arturia/MicroFreak/Idea/Rust CLI Preset Manager, which aimed to create a CLI called freakio based on Elektroid and Arturia/Forum/24/05/MIDI Control Center alternative for MicroFreak on Linux. Ok, so here's what I'm aiming for: either mise/Task/File (see also My/Pref/Dev/mise/Tasks) or a dedicated CLI which can enable AI agents to keep my Microfreak presets in sync with my knowledge garden's Microfreak/Preset area of the garden without me needing to get too involved. It's okay to download elektroid and use it if that works, or you can make a new repo with a fresh CLI that make a streamlined version of this possible in a reusable way. BTW Elektroid source code is available to you locally.

in logseq, one can click on a frontmatter item and be taken to a page. For example, preset-on-device is literally the page preset-on-device. I want to develop or work towards a convention that when frontmatter is defined in a logseq entity, then the frontmatter defined and requested by that entity should be related to the entity, for provenance and data definition reasons, and the page for the custom frontmatter attribute must be filled in with its definition - and that definition should be of type Logseq/Entity/Frontmatter/Definition. There's a design tension here. If we click on a certain property, say, preset-on-device, we are taken to a page that is not a subnamespace of Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth the way that definition page describes. One way around this would be to create Logseq/Entity/Preset/Frontamtter/preset-on-device with an alias of preset-on-device, so that clicking on preset-on-device would take it to the appropriate location in the garden. I think we need to further stipulate that prefixes should have a certain type of namespacing. For example, in the entity system, Logseq/Entity/X/Y/Z/Frontmatter/Fruit should likely lead to frontmatter key x-y-z-fruit. We don't need to do this everywhere just yet, but in this synth preset space, I'd like to do this.
